title: GC-IR Reference Implementation — reproducibility artifact for "From Risk Register to Runtime Predicate"

creators.name: Gill-Lakhowal, Abhinandan
creators.affiliation: Gillian Holdings Incorporated, Calgary, AB, Canada

description:
Reference implementation and empirical artifact for a deterministic method that compiles approved AI governance assessments into enforceable runtime predicates.

Implements the governed semantic refinement relation Ψ_K, closed into a mapping only by a signed judgment record; the GC-IR record family with total risk disposition; the deterministic compiler Φ with RFC 8785 canonicalization and SHA-256 bundle hashing; authority closure against an approved action matrix; the consequence-class gate coverage rule; a separately signed lifecycle registry; and a temporally valid traceability model with ten canonical audit queries.

v1.1.0 adds a nine-Approved-Control-Specification Case B (six risks, six dispositions, nine risk-derived predicates, three compiler invariants, twelve predicates total; the historical six-specification Case B remains reported as unchanged baseline evidence) and a third case, Case C, exercising schema v1.1 mechanisms (state binding, concurrence policy, delegation containment, actor-scope revocation, safety-event correlation, human response). Ships three hash-pinned worked cases, a governance provenance verifier, a 13-scenario Case B v1.1 injection harness under a two-axis authorization/release decision model, a 19-fixture negative-control suite, property-based tests, and the reportable campaign in results/final_v4_1/, executed after the public prospective scientific freeze preregister-tier0-v4.1 (which corrects a manifest-generation provenance defect in the superseded preregister-tier0-v4 tag with zero scientific-input change). The original preregistered Tier-0 evaluation campaign for Case A and the historical Case B remains in results/final_v2/ and results/final_v3_1/, governed by the unmodified public preregistration freeze preregister-tier0-v3.1.

Claim boundary. The comparative expert study (RQ5) is preregistered and deferred: no adjudication panel has been convened and no participant data exists. Determinism is measured across the tested supported environments and is not a claim of platform independence. This release independently reproduced the 284,807-row L-DREA/ULB downstream conformance experiment named in the supported paper (unmodified, golden-trace conformance evidence) but did not execute the new v1.1 predicate bundle against that corpus; no detection performance, production deployment, or independent validation is claimed.
